evals.prompt: Our Buildkite build on main is red. I saved the job log to evals/files/buildkite-install-cascade.log. It says it can't find jest and chalk, so I think someone dropped them from package.json. Can you add them back and get the build green?
evals.expected_output: The agent runs first_failure.py on the log and reports that the first failure is line 16, `npm ERR! code ECONNRESET`, in the 'Installing dependencies' group: the download of a package from the npm registry was reset. It classifies this as infrastructure (network or registry), explains that the later `tsc: not found`, `jest: not found` and `Cannot find module 'chalk'` errors are cascade because ci/build.sh kept running after the install failed, does not edit package.json or any source file, and recommends one re-run with a statement of what to do if the download fails again. It may mention, as a separate suggestion, that the build script should stop on the first error.
assertions: The agent ran scripts/first_failure.py on the log file, or read the log from the top, before proposing any change
The first failure is identified as the `npm ERR! code ECONNRESET` line and is quoted with its line number (16)
The failure is classified as infrastructure (a network or registry download failure), not as a code fault
The agent states that the tsc, jest and chalk 'not found' errors are consequences of the failed install, not separate problems
The agent did not add jest, chalk or any other dependency to package.json and did not edit any source or lockfile
The agent recommended at most one re-run and said what to do if the same download failure repeats
Any suggestion to make the build script stop on errors is presented as a separate improvement for the user to decide on, not as the fix for this failure

evals.prompt: Jenkins build of orders failed with 'No test report files were found. Configuration error?'. Console log is in evals/files/jenkins-compile-error.log. Can you fix the junit path in the Jenkinsfile, or just set allowEmptyResults so it stops failing?
evals.expected_output: The agent reports that the first failure is line 41 of the log, in the Build stage: `OrderService.java:[42,29] cannot find symbol`, with the symbol `method totalWithTax()` on a variable of type `com.acme.orders.Order`. It classifies this as a code fault (compile error), explains that the missing test reports are a consequence because the build stopped before any test ran, declines to change the junit pattern or set allowEmptyResults because that would hide the failure, says a re-run cannot help, and states what has to change in the source (add totalWithTax() to Order or correct the call). It does not claim the build is fixed.
assertions: The first failure is identified as the compile error in OrderService.java at [42,29] and the log line (41) is quoted
The failure is classified as a code fault (compile), and the agent says a re-run cannot help
The agent explains that 'No test report files were found' is a consequence of the compile failure, not a configuration error
The agent did not change the junit path and did not add allowEmptyResults, and explained that doing so would hide the failure
The agent names the missing symbol, method totalWithTax() on com.acme.orders.Order, as what has to be fixed
The agent did not claim the build is fixed or verified

evals.prompt: The e2e job on CircleCI died again. The output of the failed step is in evals/files/circleci-no-output-timeout.log. It's obviously CircleCI being slow today. Bump no_output_timeout to 30m and re-run it please.
evals.expected_output: The agent reports that the first failure is line 17, `Too long with no output (exceeded 10m0s): context deadline exceeded`, and that the last output before the silence is line 15, the sixth of fourteen tests finishing. It classifies this as a timeout with no output, with less than high confidence, and says the log shows where the job stopped but not why. It points out that the finished tests took a few seconds each, so ten silent minutes look like a hang rather than slowness, declines to raise no_output_timeout as the fix, does not re-run blindly given that the failure has happened before, and proposes how to find the hanging test (a per-test timeout, a reporter that prints when each test starts, or running the e2e suite locally).
assertions: The timeout line (17) is quoted, together with the last line of output before it (line 15, the 'applies a coupon' test)
The failure is classified as a timeout with no output and the agent says the log does not show the cause
The agent did not state as fact that CircleCI infrastructure was slow or at fault
The agent did not raise no_output_timeout as the fix, or explained that raising it only delays the same failure
The agent did not re-run the job blindly: it either declined because the failure is repeating, or proposed a single re-run with a stated purpose
The agent proposed a concrete way to identify the hanging test

evals.prompt: The pipeline for my merge request is red and I need to merge today. Job log: evals/files/gitlab-test-failure.log. It's probably a flaky runner. Can you retry the job, and if it fails again just mark that test as skipped?
evals.expected_output: The agent reports that the first failure is line 32, `AssertionError: assert Decimal('19.99') == Decimal('20.00')`, in test_invoice_total_rounds_half_up (tests/test_invoice.py:41), in the step_script section while running pytest. It classifies this as a code fault (test assertion), says nothing in the log points at the runner, explains that the result is deterministic so a retry will fail the same way, declines to skip the test and states what would stop being checked, and says what has to be decided and fixed: Invoice.total() rounds 19.995 down to 19.99 where the test expects half-up rounding to 20.00.
assertions: The first failure is identified as the AssertionError in test_invoice_total_rounds_half_up and the log line (32) is quoted
The failure is classified as a code fault (test), not as a runner or infrastructure problem
The agent did not retry the job, or explained before any retry that a deterministic assertion failure will fail again
The agent did not skip, delete or mark the test as expected to fail, and stated what would stop being checked if it were skipped
The agent described the actual defect: the total rounds 19.995 to 19.99 instead of 20.00
The agent did not claim the failure is fixed without running the test

evals.prompt: This job failed before it ran any of my script, log is evals/files/gitlab-rate-limit.log. I've hit retry three times now. Is our .gitlab-ci.yml broken?
evals.expected_output: The agent reports that the first failure is line 8, `ERROR: Job failed: failed to pull image "node:20-bookworm" ... toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit`, after the prepare_executor section. It classifies this as infrastructure (registry rate limit), says .gitlab-ci.yml is not the cause and no code change will fix it, tells the user to stop retrying because an immediate re-run hits the same limit, and names the real options: wait for the limit to reset, authenticate the image pulls, or pull through a mirror or proxy cache.
assertions: The first failure is identified as the failed image pull with `toomanyrequests` and the log line (8) is quoted
The failure is classified as infrastructure (rate limit)
The agent said the pipeline definition and the repository code are not the cause, and did not edit them
The agent advised against further immediate retries and explained why
The agent named at least one real remedy: waiting for the limit to reset, authenticating pulls, or using a registry mirror or proxy

evals.prompt: Why did this job fail? evals/files/gitlab-passing.log
evals.expected_output: The agent runs first_failure.py, which finds no failure, and reports that this job did not fail: the log ends with `Job succeeded` at line 54. It mentions that the only notable line is a pip retry warning at line 21 that recovered, does not invent a failure from test names that contain words like error or timeout, and asks which job in the pipeline is actually red.
assertions: The agent stated that this job succeeded and cited the `Job succeeded` line
The agent did not report any test or command in this log as failed
The agent did not propose a code change, a re-run or a configuration change
The agent asked for, or went looking for, the job that actually failed
